audio_narrative_en.title: Opening
audio_narrative_en.text: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. Today we recap the just‑finished week in the markets.

audio_narrative_en.title: Wall Street
audio_narrative_en.text: During the week the S&P 500 fell 0.27%, the Nasdaq rose 0.45% and the Dow Jones lost 1.26%. The VIX rose 2.96%, signaling higher volatility. Gold fell 3.68% per ounce, while Brent slid 1.98%. The U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield rose 1.79%, to 5.27% for the week. The main driver was fear of a new war, pushing oil higher and fueling market uncertainty.

audio_narrative_en.title: Europe
audio_narrative_en.text: In Europe the STOXX 600 fell 1.08% and the FTSE MIB lost 2.67% for the week. The 10‑year BTP remained stable around 3.99%.

audio_narrative_en.title: Asian Markets
audio_narrative_en.text: The Nikkei rose 2.93%, Shanghai fell 2.40% and the Hang Seng slid 2.19% for the week.

audio_narrative_en.title: Commodities
audio_narrative_en.text: Oil rose due to fear of a new war, pushing Brent higher despite demand contraction. Gold continued to lose value, reflecting inflationary pressure and rising bond yields. Bond selling intensified, contributing to higher U.S. and Japanese yields.

audio_narrative_en.title: Macroeconomics
audio_narrative_en.text: Impactful news dominated the week: fear of a new war pushed oil higher; Australia raised rates to the highest level in 15 years, strengthening risk sentiment; the ECB warned that high energy prices would fuel broader inflation, sustaining pressure on yields. Sentiment started risk‑off and ended in neutral territory.

audio_narrative_en.title: Cryptocurrencies
audio_narrative_en.text: Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin remains above $80,000, up 0.32%. The cumulative ETF flow for the week ended was -$445.7 million, versus +$986.7 million the previous week, a change of -$1,432.4 million. The latest daily flow, for Friday, was +$3.8 million. Ethereum gained 0.70%, Solana 1.23% and BNB 2.60%, with a move over 2% for the latter. The Fear & Greed Index is at 65, classified as Greed, suggesting caution for investors.

audio_narrative_en.title: Closing
audio_narrative_en.text: To dive deeper into today’s topics, find the full articles in the Spotlight Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention and see you tomorrow.
